definitions.explanation: Having an innocent, pure quality typically associated with young children; lacking worldliness or guile.

examples.japanese: あどけない{笑顔|えがお}の{子供|こども}たちが{遊|あそ}んでいた。
examples.english: Children with innocent smiles were playing.

examples.japanese: まだあどけない{表情|ひょうじょう}が{残|のこ}っている。
examples.english: There's still an innocent expression remaining (on their face).

examples.japanese: あどけない{目|め}で{見|み}つめられた。
examples.english: I was gazed at with innocent eyes.

notes:
CONJUGATION:
・あどけない → あどけなく (adverbial)
・あどけない → あどけなくない (negative)
・あどけない → あどけなかった (past)
・あどけない → あどけなさ (noun form)

USAGE:
Typically describes children or young people, or adults who have retained a childlike quality. Often used positively to describe a pure, unspoiled quality.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・あどけない{笑顔|えがお} (innocent smile)
・あどけない{表情|ひょうじょう} (innocent expression)
・あどけない{顔|かお} (innocent face)
・あどけない{寝顔|ねがお} (innocent sleeping face)

NUANCE:
Carries a warm, affectionate tone. Unlike {無邪気|むじゃき} (innocent/naive), あどけない specifically emphasizes the visual appearance of innocence.
